narrative.text: I’ll verify the fork baseline and test counts, resolve the upstream merge while preserving the fork’s features, then run the required gates on the local merge commit. I won’t push.Both Node versions passed the fork baseline: 795 passed, 0 failed, 28 skipped (823 total). The merge has the two expected conflicts: I’ll combine upstream’s startup parser with the fork’s configuration wiring, and retain both upstream’s clock import and the fork’s adapter imports.The combined suite exposed one additional integration issue: upstream’s shared-process test runner revealed a fork test that leaked a mocked `fetch` into upload tests. I’ve changed that test to replace its existing mock’s implementation instead of stacking mocks, preserving upstream’s runner change and the upload assertions.The merge commit is `3152457a48eb3ffe637c657f2f1d2fcf1db8c42c`, with the exact requested parents, identity, and message. All required gates passed on Node 22.23.3 and 22.12.0: 805 passed, 0 failed, 28 skipped—10 more passes than baseline. A targeted Node 24 run also passed all 91 tests, including the recipient-routing cases skipped on Node 22. I’m recording the results and finalizing; nothing was pushed.
